chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, that he was asked about the man to whom death approaches, so he divorces his wife, is her divorce valid?
He said: Yes, and if he dies, she inherits him, and if she dies, he does not inherit her.

key_terms.يَحْضُرُهُ الْمَوْتُ: approaching death / in the throes of death

ai.seo_question: Does a divorce issued by a dying man remain valid and affect inheritance rights?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling of *marad al-mawt* (deathbed) divorce, affirming its validity even if the husband dies immediately after pronouncing it. It establishes a unique asymmetry in inheritance: the divorced wife retains the right to inherit from her ex-husband upon his death, whereas he forfeits the right to inherit from her if she predeceases him, reflecting the specific legal status of the waiting period (*iddah*) in this context. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing deathbed divorce from standard divorce regarding property distribution.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,
(It has been narrated) who asked about the man to whom death approached, so he divorced his wife. Is his divorce allowed?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and if he dies, she would inherit him, and if she dies, he would not inherit her’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who is about to die, and he divorces his wife; if such divorce is permissible.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is permissible and if he dies she inherits his legacy but if she dies he does not inherit her legacy.’”
